dialogues.speaker: Tang Wen
dialogues.text: I'm thinking of the current situation of Inazuma and the Raiden Shogun's policies...

dialogues.speaker: Tang Wen
dialogues.text: I couldn't return to my hometown to see the Rite of Parting due to the Sakoku Decree, but somehow, I also happened to witness a turning point in Inazuma's history.

dialogues.speaker: Tang Wen
dialogues.text: Ah, I'm so sorry. I forgot to mention that I'm a historian from Liyue. Although I can't go home for now, I did get a chance to document the change of policy in Inazuma. It's been such a blessing in disguise.

dialogues.speaker: Tang Wen
dialogues.text: Hmm... About these policies. I still cannot come up with a final conclusion. I think that in order for us to judge a piece of history, we must document it completely first.

dialogues.speaker: Tang Wen
dialogues.text: Therefore, I have decided to stay here for a while and witness future developments in Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Tang Wen
dialogues.text: Goodbye. Perhaps we shall all witness history yet.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What was Inazuma like before?

dialogues.speaker: Tang Wen
dialogues.text: I think using words like happy or joyful to describe the Inazuma locals back then isn't really accurate... A more appropriate word would be "vigorous."

dialogues.speaker: Tang Wen
dialogues.text: The Inazuma locals before the lockdown would still worry about life's troubles. However, they had a vigor then that cannot be matched now.

dialogues.speaker: Tang Wen
dialogues.text: People are indeed living stable and peaceful lives, but if you look at the closed borders, the closed shops, and the patrolling samurai who go around seizing Visions... I don't think that anyone can feel at ease in such an oppressive situation.

dialogues.speaker: Tang Wen
dialogues.text: And this is not to mention those people whose life took a drastic turn after they lost their Visions.

dialogues.speaker: Tang Wen
dialogues.text: Does the Raiden Shogun, who seeks Eternity, really desire an Inazuma that looks like this...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, what have you heard about the Rite of Parting?

dialogues.speaker: Tang Wen
dialogues.text: To be honest, I was really terrified when I learned about Rex Lapis' passing in a letter from Liyue...

dialogues.speaker: Tang Wen
dialogues.text: Aside from being shocked, I also somehow felt regret that I was not in Liyue at such a crucial moment.

dialogues.speaker: Tang Wen
dialogues.text: I could only write to my family and my fellow researchers, asking them to document what happened at that time...

dialogues.speaker: Tang Wen
dialogues.text: Ah, Rex Lapis lived through thousands of years. If he were still around and saw what's happened in Inazuma, I wonder what he would say...

dialogues.text: Ever since the Sakoku Decree was abolished, I can feel "life" returning to Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Tang Wen
dialogues.text: You can see it on people's faces, the way they once again shine with a happiness that can only come from within.

dialogues.speaker: Tang Wen
